title: SRE Documentation Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Reviews, Operational Tooling and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE documentation standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbooks. The goal is to create consistent, searchable, and actionable documents that enable on-call success, predictable capacity, and continuous reliability improvement.

Audience:
Primary: SREs, platform engineers, and service owners. Secondary: product and infra engineers, support, and leadership.

Scope:
Applies to all externally or internally-facing services run by Redwood Inference including runtime services, control-plane APIs, ingestion pipelines, and customer-facing consoles.

SLOs and Error Budgets

1. SLO Definition Standards
- Every service must have at least one primary SLO aligned to user experience (e.g., 99.9% successful requests per minute, p95 latency < 250ms for short tail RPCs).
- SLOs must be defined in user-impact terms (availability, latency, correctness) and include the measurement window (rolling 30d, 7d, 1d as appropriate).
- SLO name format: <service>-<metric>-<window>-<target> (e.g., runtime-inference-p95-30d-250ms).
- Measurement sources must be listed and linked (Prometheus recording rules, logs-based metrics, synthetic checks).

2. Error Budget Policy
- Error budget = 1 - SLO target (e.g., 0.1% monthly allowance for 99.9%).
- Document the consumed budget, burn rate, current projection, and escalation policy in the SLO page.
- Burn rate thresholds and actions:
  - Burn rate < 1x: monitor.
  - Burn rate 1x-4x: notify service owner and schedule a reliability review within 3 business days.
  - Burn rate > 4x: urgent incident review and rollout freeze; paging to SRE lead and service owner.
- Include planned maintenance accounting rules and pre-approval workflows.

3. Ownership and Review Cadence
- SLO owner: name of the on-call team or product engineer.
- Quarterly SLO review: verify targets still match customer expectations and cost tradeoffs.
- Add an SLO change record with reason, rollback criteria, and approval reviewers.

Capacity Planning

1. Capacity Planning Document Requirements
- Each service must have a capacity planning doc containing: current capacity (instances/GPU pools), utilization trends (30/90/365d), forecasting assumptions, scaling policies, and mitigation playbooks for hot spots.
- Provide a RAG summary: Red (>90% sustained utilization), Amber (70-90%), Green (<70%).

2. Forecasting and Headroom
- Use the standard forecasting template (attached below). Forecasts should include best-case, expected, and stress-case scenarios with assumed traffic growth rates and model-sequence length distributions.
- Minimum headroom target by service tier:
  - P0 (customer-critical): 30% spare capacity sustained.
  - P1 (important infra): 25%.
  - P2/P3: 15-20%.

3. Scaling and Autoscaling Policies
- Capture autoscaling knobs and thresholds (CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, token backlog). Provide safe ramp-up policies and cool-down periods.
- Document burst capacity sources (burst pools, regional failover) and activation steps.

Reliability Initiatives (RCA -> Action)

1. Initiative Lifecycle
- Reliability initiative proposal must include: summary, affected services, impact metrics, success criteria, owners, timeline, and rollout plan.
- Prioritize initiatives based on expected reduction in error budget consumption, customer impact, or cost-to-fix ROI.

2. Tracking and Measurement
- Track initiatives in the reliability board (link) with clear metrics: pre/post SLO, mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to recover (MTTR), and cost delta.
- Each initiative must declare an evaluation window (30-90 days) and sign-off criteria.

Incident Review Standards

1. Post-Incident Review (PIR) Template
- Title, Sev level, timeline (UTC), summary, impact (customers, internal), RCA, contributing factors, mitigations, long-term actions, owner for each action, and SLA/economics impact.
- PIRs must be written within 7 days of incident mitigation for Sev>2; within 14 days for Sev 2.
- Use a blameless, systemic focus: identify process or system gaps and propose concrete changes.

2. Severity and Communication
- Severity definitions must be documented per service; default severities: Sev1 (service down/major outage), Sev2 (severe degradation affecting customers), Sev3 (partial impact), Sev4 (minor).
- Communication checklist: page on-call, update status page, notify account teams for customer impact, and schedule PIR.

3. Action Tracking and Closure
- Actions resulting from PIRs must have owners, due dates, and Be added to the reliability initiative backlog. Follow-up audits are required for high-impact actions at 30/90 days.

Operational Tooling

1. Required Tooling and Dashboards
- Standard dashboard set per service:
  - SLO dashboard (error budget, burn rate, windowed SLOs)
  - Health dashboard (request rates, 5xx counts, latency histograms, queue lengths, GPU utilization)
  - Cost and capacity dashboard (token/sec cost, reserved vs spot usage, autoscaler events)
- Link templates and dashboard JSONs in the doc. Dashboards should use consistent naming and tags (team:eng-sre, service:<service-name>).

2. Alerts and Runbook Integration
- Alerts must map to runbooks with clear severity mapping and runbook steps. Avoid alert fatigue by using aggregated symptoms and multi-tier thresholds.
- Required alerts: SLO burn rate > 1x across 30m, sustained p95 latency above threshold for 10m, GPU OOM rates above 0.5% over 1h.

3. Tooling Ownership and Access
- Define owners for observability stack (dashboards, recording rules), CI pipelines that produce metrics, and cost tooling.
- Access controls: RBAC for dashboard edits; read-only by default. Sensitive dashboards (security, customer data) marked as restricted.

SRE Runbook Standards and Template

1. Runbook Format
- Runbooks are operational playbooks used during incidents and routine ops. Each runbook must include: name, purpose, owner, on-call role to page, pre-reqs, trigger conditions, step-by-step run steps, verification steps, rollback, post-incident notes, and references.
- File name format: runbook-<service>-<short-desc>-v<major>. (e.g., runbook-runtime-kvcache-eviction-v1.json)

2. Runbook Content Requirements
- Actionable steps with commands, expected outputs, and approximate time-to-complete.
- Clearly marked manual steps versus automated remediation.
- Safety checks: who may execute destructive steps and the required approvals.

3. Example Runbook Snippet
- Title: Evict stale KV cache on runtime-node
- Trigger: sustained p95 latency > 500ms and kvcache_hit_rate < 60% for 15m
- Quick steps:
  1) Identify impacted nodes: curl -sS https://monitoring/api/alerts?service=runtime | jq '.nodes'
  2) Put node in maintenance: ./infra-cli drain-node --node $NODE --reason "kvcache-evict"
  3) Run eviction script: ssh $NODE 'sudo /opt/runtime/bin/kvcache-evict --max-age 2h'
  4) Verify hit rate improves to >75% in 10m: watch -n30 curl -sS https://monitoring/api/metrics?node=$NODE | jq '.kvcache_hit_rate'
  5) Exit maintenance and monitor for 30m.

Documentation Lifecycle and Governance

1. Templates and Storage
- All SRE docs must use the Confluence templates for SLOs, capacity plans, PIRs, runbooks, and initiatives. Store runbooks in the runbooks directory and link to the canonical Confluence page.

2. Reviews and Ownership
- Documentation owner must review runbooks and SLOs at least every 6 months and after any production incident.
- Documentation changes that affect runbook playbooks or SLO targets require reviewers including SRE lead and the service owner.

3. Audits
- Annual documentation audit: randomly sample 20% of active services for runbook completeness, accuracy of thresholds, and valid owners. Report findings to eng leadership.

Appendices

A. SLO Example Table (copy into Confluence table)
- Service: runtime-inference
- Metric: p95 latency (short-tail requests)
- Target: 99.5% requests under 250ms over 30d
- Measurement: prom_recording_rule: runtime:request_latency_p95:rate30d
- Owner: runtime-service-team
- Escalation: page SRE on-call if burn rate > 4x

B. Capacity Forecast Template (short)
- Current capacity: 1200 vGPU-accelerators (fleet split eu-west-1:40%, us-west-2:50%, ap-southeast-1:10%)
- Monthly growth: 8%
- Expected headroom required (P0): 30%
- Forecast month+3: 1200 * (1.08^3) ≈ 1520 vGPU needed -> procurement trigger

C. Runbook Checklist for Authors
- Is the runbook actionable under 15 minutes?
- Are commands copy/paste ready and tested?
- Are safety/approval steps clearly called out?
- Is monitoring verification included?
